topics: tuning knobs: batching, kv cache, quantization profile
transcript: 00:00 Evan: ok, hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Evan from Redwood, im the AE on the account, i'll kick off real quick 00:07 Evan: agenda — quick status, share the latest numbers from our lab, Sophie will walk tuning notes, then we'll triage any blockers and agree next steps 00:17 Dr. Amina: thanks, Evan, and thanks team, running late on our side, Marco will drive infra notes, Janelle on security 00:25 Sophie: hi all, Sophie here, SE, i'll be the hands on deck for the bench runs 00:30 Marco: yo, quick note — Kevin's on for recording and to capture config, apologies for background 00:35 Evan: no worries — jumping into numbers, slide deck in chat, main callout: for the summarization workload (avg input length ~420 tokens) our run shows p50 of 82 ms, p95 of 260 ms, p99 ~540 ms, throughput sustained at 240 rps at 16 concurrent streams 00:55 Dr. Amina: sorry say that again p95 260? our incumbent vendor had p95 around 480 in our tests 01:02 Evan: yes that's right, incumbent vendor numbers are what RidgePoint shared — about p95 480 and top-end 900 p99 for some bursts, and throughput was peaking at ~150 rps before queuing 01:15 Marco: can you confirm test env parity — GPU type, batch settings? we tried to mirror but might be off 01:21 Sophie: good question, we used A100-40 in our hosted lab, quantization FP16 paths, batch size auto with Redwood's adaptive batching, KV cache enabled for prefix reuse — i'll put exact config in the export 01:35 Marco: ah we used V100 on the incumbent side, so some difference expected — but still those latency deltas are material 01:42 Janelle: on security, quick question: did you store any payload in the KV cache persistently? we need to know for data retention policies 01:49 Sophie: KV cache is ephemeral in our runs, in prod we offer optional prefix caching but it's scrubbed per tenant by default, not persisted to disk 01:58 Janelle: ok please follow up with docs, SOC2 related, and KMS integration details 02:05 Evan: noted, we'll attach our security pack, Sophie can send the KMS notes 02:10 Kevin (intern): um small thing — the graphs look smoothed, can we get raw traces? 02:13 Sophie: yes we'll include raw histograms and the per-request logs, that's part of the next deliverable 02:18 Dr. Amina: about throughput — you mentioned 240 rps at 16 streams, our production will be bursty, more like spikes of 250-300 for short periods 02:28 Sophie: burst behavior is where auto-burst and dedicated capacity tradeoffs come in — hosted will handle medium bursts with some queueing but dedicated reserved pools give predictable headroom 02:38 Marco: cost side — what are implications moving from hosted to dedicated, ballpark? our finops will need numbers 02:44 Evan: rough ballpark: dedicated (reserved) for the peak profile you're describing tends to be a ~20-25% higher fixed cost but reduces per-token marginal cost by ~30% due to caching and batching efficiencies. we'll send a detailed cost model 02:58 Dr. Amina: ok please include an example monthly invoice split, that helps procurement 03:04 Evan: will do, we'll model based on your historical token counts 03:09 Sophie: back to tuning — practical levers we adjusted this week: 1) decreased auto-batch window from 25ms to 12ms for lower tail latency 2) tuned KV eviction to favor prefix reuse across identical sessions 3) swapped to a quantization profile that favors faster matmul kernels at slight fp rounding 03:25 Marco: did that change throughput? seems like lower window may reduce batching efficiency 03:29 Sophie: yes small tradeoff — p50 improved ~10%, p95 improved more due to fewer queued inputs, throughput measured steady dropped 5% but effective latency under load was better; we can run a dedicated slot to try different windows 03:42 Dr. Amina: Sophie, when you say quantization profile that favours faster kernels, any impact on output quality? we've had hallucination concerns in summaries 03:50 Sophie: we ran BLEU/ROUGE parity checks on a sample set — no significant regressions, but we'll include the eval diffs, still recommend keeping full-precision for the most sensitive prompts 03:59 Marco: also curious about long context sessions — we have some flows that keep a rolling 8k context, how did cache behave? 04:06 Sophie: KV cache reuse showed ~35% token save on that flow, latency for repeated prefixes dropped 40% — i'll add the per-flow breakdown 04:16 Janelle: encryption at rest — for dedicated deployments can you integrate customer KMS or must we use Redwood-managed keys? 04:23 Evan: in Redwood Private/dedicated we support customer-managed KMS for keys, in hosted we provide optional KMS integration with bring-your-own-key patterns for enterprise tiers 04:32 Janelle: ok record that, Mark from legal will want the key rotation policy 04:37 Dr. Amina: i'm worried about the 'incumbent' having more regional presence — can Redwood route to regions? we need eu data residency 04:44 Evan: yes we have region routing policies, and private can be deployed in eu-west regions, can also pin model versions and routing rules 04:51 Marco: quick nit: earlier in the deck i saw references to 'KV cash' — i think that's a transcription artifact in the doc, please fix 04:58 Sophie: haha noted, we'll correct typos 05:02 Kevin (intern): oh also question about warmup — how long to warm caches when promoting a model? 05:08 Sophie: depends on workload, typical warmup for 8k context flow is 10-30 minutes under synthetic warmup traffic, but for production ramp we recommend canary and gradual traffic shifting 05:18 Dr. Amina: thanks that's helpful — timeline wise we're targetting decision by end of month, procurement wants one more head-to-head with dedicated runs 05:25 Evan: perfect, Sophie will schedule a dedicated 2-hour slot next week and run parity configs vs incumbent as you requested 05:31 Sophie: yes propose Thursday 2026-03-25 09:00-11:00 PT, we'll run a 16-concurrency sustained run and capture 1s granularity traces 05:40 Marco: that works, i'll unblock infra and provide networking access and test creds 05:45 Janelle: Security will be on call for the dedicated run, we'll watch for any egress or unexpected logs 05:51 Evan: recap — actions: we send raw traces and config diffs, schedule dedicated slot (Sophie), RidgePoint to share production prompt set and SLOs (Amina), Janelle to share SOC2 contact and KMS constraints 05:59 Dr. Amina: good — one more ask, include the comparison sheet with the incumbent's numbers side-by-side so it's easy for our execs 06:05 Evan: will include a side-by-side CSV and cost modeling 06:10 Sophie: i'll also include a short runbook for the dedicated test so we can reproduce locally if needed 06:15 Evan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and slack, action items in the doc, talk soon 06:20 Meeting end
